IMPLEMENT STORY #832: engine: a boxed exec dispatch under namespace is not held to its pinned script bytes at spawn

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-832-boxed-rewalk, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (on a branch from before #423, PR #544, the old form is --test suppressions), and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it suppressions:: (since #423, each crate's integration tests are one binary, run as --test it FILE::, and a new tests/*.rs is registered as mod FILE; in its crate's tests/it.rs, which layering::test_targets enforces; on a branch from before #423 the old --test FILE forms stand)
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending: this seat is non-interactive, so ending the turn ends the process and your result file is never written.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#832)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- The implement phase alone changes files and commits. Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY whatever this text asks elsewhere: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit; it reports each finding, and a returned finding is fixed by the implementer in a later round.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.
- When a test fails, keep its whole failure text: do not filter cargo test output through grep or tail before reading it, and quote the panic message (and any cause line it prints) in your notes, even for a failure you judge a flake in code you did not touch.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is origin/main as you find it (fe0eedee or later). Main lands only through the merge queue. THIS BRANCH IS STACKED: story-832-boxed-rewalk is cut from story-823-rewalk at 2171e268 (#823, PR #836, in the merge queue), which sits on main fe0eedee. Do not merge or rebase: the controller rebases this branch onto main after #836 merges.
- THIS STORY IS #832 as the operator ruled it. 2026-10-22, in chat, verbatim: "accept all". Recorded on #832 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/832#issuecomment-6334785922). It takes option (a): a boxed exec dispatch, a site with `hands` under the `namespace` boundary, is re-walked at spawn as an unboxed one is. `compose_segments`' Namespace arm sets `rewalk` from the same typed dispatch, and `layer_drift` refuses an edited, removed or added file BEFORE the box is built, with decision 0048's existing text, naming the layer. That is one derivation for both boundaries (decision 0071 ruling 5). No witness digest moves. Options (b) (a snapshot of the pinned layer mounted into the box) and (c) (accept and document) were NOT taken: do not build them.
- Also binding: 2026-10-21, "823 a" (every exec dispatch whose script is pinned in a compiled layer is re-walked at spawn). Decision 0046 ruling 4. Decision 0048 ruling 2. 2026-09-26, the threat model (catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read). Decision 0071 rulings 3, 5, 8 and 9.
- WHERE THE CODE IS (on 2171e268, #823's head; verify each anchor):
  - crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs `compose_segments`: the unboxed branch (`boundary != BuiltBoundary::Namespace && is_exec_dispatch(..)`) and, since #823, the hands-less return set `rewalk` through the one helper #823 made, which derives the script from `crate::argv::Dispatch::of(argv)`'s exec tail (no positional skip). The `BuiltBoundary::Namespace` arm calls `hands_command(command, Some(spec), workdir, boxed, roots)` and returns `SiteSpawn::of(behind(mapped, &segments))` with `rewalk` None.
  - crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/dispatch.rs (about :399-406): `if let Some(layer) = &spawn.rewalk` then `layer_drift(bundle, layer)`, refusing "unboxed exec dispatch refused: layer '{layer}' moved since the compile ({key}); ...". That runs before `DriverProcess` spawns, so before any box is built.
  - The box mounts the bundle root read-only from the host (crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands.rs about :374-377, `Mount::RoBind`). `hands_command` (engine/boxed.rs) maps the argv's tokens into the box's paths.
- THE CHANGE:
  1. The Namespace arm sets `rewalk` from the ORIGINAL, host-side command, the same helper's answer on the compiled argv, before `hands_command` maps it into the box's paths. The walk compares host files with the compiled map.
  2. The refusal text: today's says "unboxed exec dispatch refused: ...", which is false for a boxed site. Decision 0048's text should stay exact for unboxed sites (their tests pin it). For a boxed one, word it truthfully in the same form: "boxed exec dispatch refused: layer '{layer}' moved since the compile ({key}); the bytes a gate runs must be the bytes its digest names (decision 0046 ruling 4, decision 0048, #832)", or close to it. Choose from the spawn's boundary, quote the exact text in your notes, and say why. This is new user-facing text, so the PR names it.
  3. The other arms (Harness and Open model seats, inline sites with no candidate) do not change. A model seat is not an exec dispatch.
- TESTS (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/boundary_tests.rs or its rewalk child; exact strings, each with a removal control):
  1. a boxed exec site (hands, `namespace`) whose script in the LEAF layer is edited after the compile is refused at spawn with the exact boxed text, and no box process starts;
  2. the same for a script in an ANCESTOR layer of a composed bundle;
  3. a file removed, and a file added, in the walked directory: each refused with "missing: ..." or "added: ...";
  4. untouched: the walk passes and the spawn proceeds to the box exactly as today: the same argv, env and box spec.
  - Under namespace a real box can only be built where bwrap works and the test is not already boxed. Follow `sealed_tests`' `already_boxed()` skip. The refusal cases must not need a box at all, because they refuse before it. Run them everywhere.
  - HOST INDEPENDENCE: pin `engine.network_prefix = Some(false)` in any test that composes through `Engine::compose`. The merge queue's hosted runners pass the probe, and the workstation does not (PR #828's queue failure).
  - Removal control: drop the Namespace arm's rewalk. Tests 1 to 3 fail with the edited script started.
- EXISTING TESTS: every existing test keeps its name and assertions. If one asserts a boxed exec site's `rewalk` is None, it pinned the gap the ruling closes. Change only that assertion, to `Some(<the directory>)`, name it, and the PR's Ruling: line carries it.
- GATES:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings;
  - cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 590). engine::broker::admission tests may flake under load (#811): rerun one alone;
  - cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked -- witness_digests:: with NO re-pin and no BROKKR_BLESS;
  - cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- machine_proof:: realms:: recipes:: folder_seats:: hands:: (timeout 590): boxed runs over unedited scripts complete as before;
  - quality/ratchet.sh files (engine.rs is at its row: keep the net change at zero or below, and put any helper in an existing child module), clones, api (no public-api change);
  - cargo crap on brokkr-runtime: compose_segments and every function you change at CC 15 or under;
  - typos --hidden; git diff --check.
- DOCS: decision 0048's text and docs/guides/how-brokkr-works.md (or wherever the walk is described). If a line says a boxed site is not re-walked, or that the walk is for unboxed sites alone, update only that sentence to say what the code now does (amended by #832, operator ruling "accept all", 2026-10-22).
- CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-b9 or any brokkr-wt-* seat): decision 0065 slice two's U9a2 (bundle.rs, bundle/mcp.rs, capabilities.rs) is held for an operator ruling. #288 slice P moves engine.rs's advance_running and start_in_world into engine/cursor.rs and engine/start.rs: keep this story's engine.rs hunk to compose_segments. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs is under an operator HOLD.
- SIZE: about +15/-5 in production, about +200 in tests. One commit.

THE ISSUE (#832), verbatim:

A boxed exec dispatch, a site with `hands` under the `namespace` boundary, spawns whatever bytes its script holds at spawn time. Nothing compares them with the bytes its compile pinned. Unboxed exec dispatches are re-walked at spawn (decision 0048 ruling 2), and #823 extends that walk to hands-less ones. Under `namespace`, the same edit runs unchecked.

## Where (main fe0eedee)

- `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs` `compose_segments` (about :3036). The re-walk is set only on the `boundary != BuiltBoundary::Namespace && is_exec_dispatch(..)` branch, through `exec_segments` (`spawn.rewalk = script_directory(..)`). The `BuiltBoundary::Namespace` arm calls `hands_command` and returns `SiteSpawn::of(..)`, with `rewalk` None.
- `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/dispatch.rs:400` is `layer_drift`'s only caller. It runs only when `spawn.rewalk` is Some.
- `hands_command` (engine/boxed.rs) rewrites tokens and compares no digest.
- The box mounts the bundle root read-only from the host (`crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands.rs:374-377`, `Mount::RoBind`). A host-side edit after the compile is visible inside the box at spawn. `sealed.confirm` checks the box's reach, not the layer's bytes.

Three reviewers of #823's landing (2026-10-22, `implement-story-823-engine-an-ex-6170d830`) each confirmed this independently, and none found a path that holds the bytes.

## Why it matters

The threat model (2026-09-26) is realistic accidental misuse. With decision 0091's folder seats (#717, slice 3b merged fe0eedee), a recipe's verify can be the folder's own `.brokkr/scripts/verify-seat.sh`. Under `harness`, a work seat that rewrites that script after the compile makes the verify refuse at spawn. The 3b landing showed this end to end. Under `namespace`, the box's read-only bind keeps the box from writing the bundle root. But a host-side edit made between the compile and the spawn, such as a work seat's worktree that is the bundle's own checkout, or the operator, still reaches the spawned script, and the run goes on as if nothing changed.

Decision 0046 ruling 4: "the bytes an unboxed gate runs must be the bytes its digest names". It speaks of unboxed gates. Whether the box was meant to carry the same guarantee by other means is the question.

## Asked of the operator

- **(a), recommended:** a boxed exec dispatch is re-walked at spawn as an unboxed one is. `compose_segments`' Namespace arm sets `rewalk` from the same typed dispatch, and `layer_drift` refuses an edited, removed or added file before the box is built, with decision 0048's existing text, naming the layer. That's one derivation for both boundaries (decision 0071 ruling 5), and no witness digest moves.
- (b): the box mounts a snapshot of the pinned layer instead of the live root. That is stronger, but it means copying layers per spawn.
- (c): accept the gap, documented: under `namespace` the bundle root is trusted between compile and spawn.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
```
